stem.en: A person reasons that because a peptide supplement is legally sold online, it must have already been shown to be reasonably safe before being allowed on the market. Why is this reasoning flawed for a product marketed as a dietary supplement?
stem.et: Inimene arutleb, et kuna peptiiditoidulisandit müüakse seaduslikult veebis, peab see olema juba näidatud mõistlikult ohutuna, enne kui see turule lubati. Miks on see arutluskäik toidulisandina turundatud toote puhul vigane?

label.en: Because in most jurisdictions, a supplement manufacturer does not need to prove safety or efficacy before selling a product -- regulatory action typically only removes a product from the market after evidence of harm has already emerged.
label.et: Sest enamikus jurisdiktsioonides ei pea toidulisandi tootja tõestama ohutust ega tõhusust enne toote müümist -- regulatiivne tegevus eemaldab toote turult tavaliselt alles pärast seda, kui kahjustusest tõendid on juba ilmnenud.

label.en: The reasoning isn't flawed -- legal availability for sale as a supplement is functionally equivalent to the safety and efficacy testing a prescription medication undergoes.
label.et: Arutluskäik ei ole vigane -- seaduslik saadavus toidulisandina müügiks on funktsionaalselt samaväärne ohutuse ja tõhususe testimisega, mida retseptiravim läbib.

label.en: It's flawed only because peptide supplements specifically are always fake and contain no active ingredient at all, unlike other legally sold supplement categories.
label.et: See on vigane ainult sellepärast, et spetsiifiliselt peptiiditoidulisandid on alati võltsingud ega sisalda üldse toimeainet, erinevalt teistest seaduslikult müüdavatest toidulisandi kategooriatest.

label.en: It's flawed because the product's legal status guarantees it has no dangerous interactions with any prescription medication a buyer might already be taking.
label.et: See on vigane, kuna toote seaduslik staatus garanteerib, et sellel ei ole ohtlikke koostoimeid mistahes retseptiravimiga, mida ostja võib juba võtta.
